findings.claim: Controlled-language text alone cannot promise reduced tokens or better decisions.
findings.change: Retain the candidate's explicit unproven assumption and matched host measurements; no quantitative savings promise.
findings.rationale: The profile is a design hypothesis; current-host decisions and actual exposed usage, not file length, establish benefit.

findings.claim: Directional graph invalidation and producer proof identity may be split into independent accepted fixes.
findings.change: Keep one bounded invariant repair covering both layers and negative regressions, not separate falsely complete tasks.
findings.rationale: Schema-2 acceptance can remain stale after a graph-only fix; the smallest honest result preserves both graph and proof semantics.

findings.claim: All later-increment work must wait for the preceding increment's acceptance.
findings.change: Retain zero hard-start dependencies and actual integration/validation ordering. Runtime write/asset conflicts still constrain scheduling.
findings.rationale: Integration depends on produced behavior and acceptance depends on current prior proof; neither requires a manufactured whole-increment start gate.

findings.claim: Cumulative outcome and intent acceptance should rerun unchanged leaf proof separately.
findings.change: Retain primary composition proofs only at three gates and explicit reuse of current preceding/leaf proof.
findings.rationale: Reuse does not waive changed-source freshness or new composition; it prevents ceremonial duplicate execution.

findings.claim: A large harness footprint justifies automatic deletion of evidence.
findings.change: Retain a bounded read-only preview and explicit ownership unknowns. No GC, history rewrite or source exclusions.
findings.rationale: Observed local size is not proof that every artifact is irrelevant or safe to remove.

summary: Retain the 13-node/three-increment candidate. Each requirement has implementing and acceptance coverage; no executable work is orphaned. Gates reuse current proof but own new composition. Zero hard-start dependencies avoid invented phase locks; shared source and inspection conflicts still serialize actual writes. Post-change assurance and release controls remain incomplete.
limitations: This review is from the planning agent, not a separately authorized independent sub-agent.
Behavior defects require actual failing-before reproductions in TASK-411; static source and baseline tests do not supply them.
Matched host/token qualification, current post-change assurance and release controls are not completed.
Candidate write scopes bound possible change, not a mandate to edit every matched file; no broad cosmetic rewording is authorized.
